title: Lemma `lem:Cc-iso`: support/compactness correspondence asserted in one phrase

comments.author: human
comments.body:
In `lem:Cc-iso` (§1) the isomorphism $\mathcal C_c^\infty(N_{n+1}\backslash P_{n+1},\psi^{-1})\cong\mathcal C_c^\infty(N_n\backslash\mathrm{GL}_n,\psi^{-1})$ is established, and the algebraic bijection plus the $\psi(-Q\,g_{nn})$ twist are verified correctly. The single under-justified step is the assertion: "Smoothness and the compact-support condition correspond under the identification $N_{n+1}\backslash P_{n+1}=N_n\backslash\mathrm{GL}_n$."

Because the fibre of $P_{n+1}\to\mathrm{GL}_n$ is the **non-compact** group $F^n$, this needs an explicit argument. The correct reason is the explicit formula $f((h,v))=\psi(-v_n)\,F(h)$: the $(N_{n+1},\psi^{-1})$-equivariance forces the entire $v$-dependence to be the unitary character $\psi(-v_n)$, so there is *no* support condition in the $v$-direction. Consequently $\operatorname{supp} f$ is compact modulo $N_{n+1}$ **iff** $\operatorname{supp} F$ is compact modulo $N_n$. This should be written out, since naively a function on a space with non-compact fibres need not have compact-mod-$N_{n+1}$ support even if its restriction does.
